messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: NCCL allreduce timeouts and kv-cache memory runaway on tp-32 pools in us-east-1 observed at 1904999900. Error spike correlates with continuous_batching_v4 rollout. PD: https://pd.example/INC-30077

sam-oncall: i'm on it. creating a temporary war-room. initial symptoms? which endpoints are blowing up?

devin: streaming and long-context generation endpoints are the worst. continuous-batching queue depth is exploding and per-shard kv cache entries show a bimodal distribution. logs include repeated stacktraces: `kv_cache: eviction loop unable to catch up` and `nccl: allreduce timed out (rank 3)`.

ariya: metrics: tp-32 NCCL stall p50: 45ms -> p50: 1.8s, p95: >3s. memory pressure on some devices hit 92%. This aligns with sequences of mixed lengths being batched into the same cross-device batches.

leo: quick theory: continuous_batching_v4 introduced a seq-hash sharder that uses sequence prefix + hash to assign keys; it appears to create hotspots when requests with certain prefixes concentrate on a few shards. combined with bigger batch windows this leads to cross-shard KV cache duplication and evictions.

sam-oncall: actions: 1) reduce customer impact, 2) apply hot mitigations, 3) prepare safe rollback. Who can apply the hotpatch?

ops-bot: runbook-kv-cache: https://runbooks.example/kv-cache-hotpath. Suggested immediate mitigations: reduce batch window, disable seq-hash sharder, increase eviction aggressiveness, optionally replicate hot prefixes.

devin: I'm going to reduce batching window and enable aggressive eviction first. commands: 
```
# tighten batch window and backpressure
redwoodctl override set --pool tp-32 continuous_batching.max_window_ms=6
redwoodctl override set --pool tp-32 continuous_batching.global_backpressure=0.75
# make eviction more aggressive
redwoodctl override set --pool tp-32 kv_cache.eviction_target_percent=0.55
```

ariya: applying now. small rollback visible in metrics already: queue depth down ~40% in 30s. but NCCL stalls still happening on nodes with very skewed shard distributions.

leo: for the stubborn nodes we should disable the seq-hash sharder and fall back to modulo sharding to rebalance keys across devices. this will avoid the pathological prefix clustering.

sam-oncall: agree. devin, can you roll that change? keep the rollout rolling with low parallelism.

devin: doing it. 
```
# revert sharder to modulo for tp-32 pools
redwoodctl config set --pool tp-32 runtime.tp_kv_sharder.mode=modulo --env prod
redwoodctl rollout restart --pool tp-32 --strategy rolling --parallel 2
```

clara: CS update: acct-Delta and acct-Beta reported increased timeouts. i've notified them and created support tickets. sending a holding message now: "We're investigating increased latency and timeouts; mitigation in progress."

support: sent to acct-Delta + acct-Beta. requesting logs & sample request ids for their affected calls.

ariya: after first two nodes restarted with modulo sharder, NCCL timeouts dropped ~70% on those nodes. replication not required yet. overall p95 recovered to near baseline but p99 still elevated for streaming.

leo: for nodes where shard skew > 2x, apply temporary replicate-hot-prefixes to avoid cross-device fetches for hot keys. this is heavier on memory but lowers cross-GPU comms. command: 
```
redwoodctl override set --asg ng-tp32-az2 tp_kv_sharder.replicate_prefixes='["/v1/stream/", "/v1/chat/"]'
```

devin: applied to ng-tp32-az2. memory used up ~10% on that ASG but streaming p99 improved quickly. I'm marking the hotpatch applied.

sam-oncall: good. ops-bot, tag this incident as P1 and list affected customers.

ops-bot: Incident INC-30077 acknowledged by sam-oncall. Severity: P1. Affected: acct-Delta (timeouts), acct-Beta (increased latency), acct-Gamma (degraded throughput). Runbook: kv-cache-hotpath.

clara: customer comms update sent: "We've applied mitigations (reduced batching window, reverted sharder, and localized prefix replication). We expect performance recovery; post-incident RCA will follow."

devin: next on durable fix: 1) revert seq-hash sharder until we have preflight distribution checks; 2) change continuous_batching to include a per-shard backpressure factor so a single shard can't cause global queue growth; 3) add CI test simulating skewed prefix distributions and measure per-shard memory variance.

leo: i'll own the sharder rollback and add instrumentation: per-shard key counts, hot-prefix detection, and pre-deploy gate that blocks deploys if imbalance >1.3x.

ariya: i'll add NCCL stall synthetic tests to CI and a post-deploy smoke test that sends variable-length sequences to a canary pool for 5 minutes to ensure no sudden shard skew.

sam-oncall: creating follow-up ticket INC-30078 for RCA and action items. i'll hand off to runtime for 4h monitoring. i'll remain on-call for escalation. great work everyone.

ops-bot: Incident INC-30077 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem assigned to leo. Closing war-room in 10m if no regressions. :thumbsup:
